questions.q: What behavior did Wang et al.'s "Interpretability in the Wild" study in GPT-2 small?
options: Image classification accuracy
Indirect object identification -- predicting the correct name (e.g., "Mary") rather than the repeated subject ("John") in sentences like the paper's example
Sentiment analysis of movie reviews
Arithmetic addition of two-digit numbers
questions.explain: The paper studies how GPT-2 small picks the indirect object rather than re-selecting the subject, using the logit difference between the two candidate names as its metric.

questions.q: In the five-step workflow, what distinguishes testing necessity from testing sufficiency?
options: Necessity ablates the candidate circuit and checks if the behavior collapses; sufficiency patches only the candidate circuit's activations into a different run and checks if the behavior is restored
They are the same test performed twice
Sufficiency requires no forward passes through the model at all
Necessity only applies to MLP layers, sufficiency only to attention heads
questions.explain: Necessity asks "does removing it break the behavior," while sufficiency asks "does patching in just this circuit's activations restore the behavior on its own."

questions.q: Roughly how many attention heads, and across how many functional classes, did Wang et al. identify for the IOI circuit?
options: A single head with no further classification
Every head in the entire model, with no distinct classes
Exactly two heads, matching the induction-head circuit
Roughly 26-28 attention heads across about seven functional classes, including duplicate token heads, S-inhibition heads, and name mover heads
questions.explain: The paper found a multi-head, multi-class circuit -- considerably larger and more varied than the two-head induction circuit from the previous lesson.

questions.q: What does "minimality" ask about a proposed circuit explanation?
options: Whether the circuit is the smallest model architecture ever published
Whether every component included in the circuit is actually needed, or whether it could be made smaller without losing the behavior
Whether the circuit's logit difference is exactly zero
Whether the circuit uses the fewest possible lines of code
questions.explain: Minimality checks that no unnecessary components were swept into the proposed circuit -- every included piece should be pulling real weight.

questions.q: In the lesson's patching code, what does it mean if patching only the hypothesized heads' clean-run activations into a corrupted run restores most of the clean logit difference?
options: It means the hypothesis has been disproven
It has no bearing on necessity or sufficiency
It means the model's weights have been permanently altered
It is real evidence that those heads are sufficient on their own to produce the behavior, not merely correlated with it
questions.explain: Restoring the behavior by patching in only the candidate heads' activations is direct evidence of sufficiency, complementing the necessity test from ablation.
